rows.gloss: one desiring liberation, for such a one

items.question: Why should the seeker for liberation enter facing the northern direction?
premises: The one desiring liberation may enter facing the northern direction.
The fire of Aghora burns the binding bonds.
The northern direction is associated with Aghora's liberating power.
items.inference: Entering facing north aligns the seeker with Aghora's fire, which destroys the bonds of bondage.
uncertainties: The exact referent of tādṛśāya is context-dependent.
items.plain_english: There the seeker for liberation should enter facing the northern direction, for the fire of Aghora burns away the bonds that bind.

rows.gloss: any such as east, west, and so on
could be of a single one

items.question: Can directions like east and west exist independently without any limiting condition?
premises: No direction such as east or west exists as an independent entity.
There can be no cognition of a single direction without a limiting condition.
Direction depends on some imposed reference.
items.inference: Directions are not absolute realities but arise only through limiting conditions.
uncertainties: The precise philosophical sense of pratyaya here could be cognition or valid apprehension.
items.plain_english: Even though we speak of directions like east and west, there is no such thing as direction by itself, for no single direction can be cognized without a limiting condition.

rows.gloss: is taught as east and so on
if so, that is caused by it

items.question: If direction is only a limiting condition, how can it account for real variety?
premises: One might claim that direction is produced by a limiting condition such as east and so on.
A mere limiting condition is only an external designation.
A mere designation cannot by itself explain genuine variety.
items.inference: Direction cannot be adequately explained as nothing more than an external limiting condition.
uncertainties: The exact force of tatkṛtaṃ could be 'produced by that' or 'determined by that'.
items.plain_english: If someone says that direction is just a limiting condition called east and so on, then how could such a mere condition account for real variety?

rows.gloss: powerfully displaying the variety called the division of east and other directions

items.question: What is the true source of the division into east and other directions?
premises: Direction cannot be explained by mere external limiting conditions.
The light of consciousness appears in the form of manifest objects.
The division of directions is a displayed variety within manifestation.
items.inference: The division of directions arises from the light of consciousness as it appears in formed manifestation.
uncertainties: durmadaḥ is taken as intensifying 'boldly/powerfully displaying' rather than literal intoxication.
items.plain_english: Therefore it is this light of consciousness, appearing in the form of objects, that boldly displays the variety known as the division into east and other directions.

items.question: How are the directions above and below determined within the light of consciousness?
premises: Whatever is always fit to be taken up by light is experienced as above.
Whatever is unfit for contact by light is experienced as below.
Above and below are defined by degrees of luminous accessibility.
items.inference: The vertical division of directions arises from what consciousness can or cannot illuminate and grasp.
uncertainties: sparśāyogya may imply tactile contact or more generally cognitive accessibility.
items.plain_english: Whatever is always fit to be taken up by light is above, being of the nature of light, while what is unfit for contact is below.

rows.gloss: of what is fit to be slightly illuminated

items.question: How does the middle region give rise to the forward direction?
premises: What is only slightly luminous constitutes the middle.
From this middle state the differentiation of directions arises.
Light spreading toward what can be slightly illuminated defines the front.
items.inference: The forward direction emerges when consciousness extends from the middle toward what is partially illuminable.
uncertainties: The compound split in the second half follows the transmitted reading and may vary slightly by edition.
items.plain_english: What is only slightly luminous is the middle, and from that the directions arise; when light spreads toward what can be slightly illuminated, that is the front.

rows.gloss: the pair of directions has come about
having grasped it, with rays more abundant

items.question: How do front and back arise as a pair of directions?
premises: What faces toward illumination is the front.
What is turned away from illumination is the back.
Light becomes more intense when it grasps an object directly in front.
items.inference: Front and back arise as a directional pair from the orientation and intensity of illuminating consciousness.
uncertainties: udriktaraśmikaḥ is interpreted as increased intensity of light rather than a literal ray-count.
items.plain_english: What is turned away is behind, so front and back arise as a pair; when light faces an object and grasps it, its rays become more abundant.

rows.gloss: that is due to conformity with that light

items.question: How are the right and left directions determined?
premises: The right side is defined by its conformity with the direction of light.
Left and right are relational, not absolute, positions.
What stands in front of the right side is designated as the left.
items.inference: Right and left arise from the relational orientation of illuminated space.
uncertainties: The phrasing is compressed; the relational mapping is inferred from the directional logic of the passage.
items.plain_english: Where light stands in conformity, that is called the right; and what stands in front of that right side is taught to be the left.

rows.gloss: gentle through contact with the knowable moon illuminated by that light
thus in this set of four directions, through resting in the middle

items.question: How does the first set of four directions become established?
premises: The illuminated knowable can be experienced as gentle, like moonlight.
Directional differentiation proceeds from a central resting point.
The first four directions form a coherent set around that center.
items.inference: The primary four directions are established through the centered play of illuminating consciousness.
uncertainties: The image of the moon may be metaphorical for soothing luminosity rather than a ritual object.
items.plain_english: That same illuminated field, gentle like the touch of moonlight, gives rise in this way to the first set of four directions through resting in the middle.

rows.gloss: by another set of four, there are eight
directions presided over by their respective powers
in this mere light that grants boons

items.question: How do the eight directions arise within supreme Śiva?
premises: A second set of four directions combines with the first to make eight.
Each direction is presided over by a corresponding power.
All this differentiation occurs within the supreme light of Śiva.
items.inference: The full system of eight directions is a differentiated manifestation within Śiva's luminous consciousness.
uncertainties: The specific presiding powers are not named in this verse.
items.plain_english: With another set of four, the directions become eight, each presided over by its own power; all this arises within the supreme, boon-granting light of Śiva.

rows.gloss: because he has a body of five mantras

items.question: How is the division of directions grounded in both world and scripture?
premises: The division of directions is established in ordinary experience and in scripture.
Sadāśiva is taught as having a body composed of five mantras.
This fivefold form provides a scriptural basis for directional order.
items.inference: The worldly division of directions corresponds to the five-mantra form of Sadāśiva taught in scripture.
uncertainties: The verse bridges into the next explanation; the full mapping is completed in 204-206.
items.plain_english: The division of directions is established both in the world and in scripture, for Sadāśiva is taught in sequence as having a body made of five mantras.

rows.gloss: by the division into Īśāna, Aghora, Vāma, Sadyojāta, and the lower

items.question: How are the five mantra-faces correlated with the directions?
premises: The fivefold mantra body is divided into Īśāna, Aghora, Vāma, Sadyojāta, and the lower face.
Īśāna corresponds to the upward direction because of its luminosity.
The extending eastern face is identified with that luminous manifestation.
items.inference: The directional system is mapped onto Sadāśiva's five mantra-faces according to their modes of luminosity.
uncertainties: The exact syntactic link of prasāri yat is compressed in the transmitted text.
items.plain_english: By the division into Īśāna, Aghora, Vāma, Sadyojāta, and the lower face, the directions are mapped out: Īśāna is above because of its luminosity, and the extending eastern face corresponds to that light.

rows.grounds: eastern or frontal face in this mapping

rows.gloss: the fierce one is the southern

items.question: Which mantra-faces correspond to the southern, northern, and western directions?
premises: The fierce Aghora face corresponds to the south.
The gentle Vāma face corresponds to the left or northern side.
Sadyojāta, being turned away, is designated as the western face.
items.inference: The cardinal directions are assigned to mantra-faces according to their qualities and orientation.
uncertainties: The mapping of Puruṣa in this verse is compressed and depends on the surrounding context.
items.plain_english: Puruṣa is identified in this scheme, the fierce Aghora is the south, the gentle Vāma is the left, and Sadyojāta, being turned away, is designated as the west.

rows.gloss: the nether face is below because of non-luminosity
space, wind, fire, water, and earth

items.question: How do the elements relate to Sadāśiva's five faces?
premises: The lower face is associated with non-luminosity and the nether region.
The five elements are space, wind, fire, water, and earth.
Sadāśiva's faces are correlated with these elemental principles.
items.inference: The five faces of Sadāśiva encompass both directional and elemental order.
uncertainties: The verse states the correlation but does not assign each element to a specific face.
items.plain_english: The nether face is below because of its lack of luminosity, and indeed space, wind, fire, water, and earth are the faces of that Lord.

rows.gloss: is said to be made of light

items.question: Why is space identified with the luminous upper principle?
premises: Space is regarded as primary among the elements in this account.
What is primary above is described as made of light.
What is below is characterized as non-luminous.
items.inference: Space is associated with the upper, luminous pole of manifestation.
uncertainties: The contrast between upper space and lower non-luminosity is doctrinally compressed.
items.plain_english: As the primary element, space alone is said to be above and made of light, while below that same principle is clearly non-luminous.

rows.gloss: because of luminosity it is seen, therefore in this there is a set of four directions

items.question: How does the middle region yield the four directions?
premises: In the middle, what is luminous is not merely an object to be illuminated.
Nor is it simply the opposite of illumination.
Because it is visible through luminosity, it gives rise to a fourfold directional structure.
items.inference: The middle luminous field becomes the basis for the four primary directions.
uncertainties: The contrast between prakāśa and prakāśya is philosophically dense and compressed here.
items.plain_english: In the middle, what is luminous is neither merely something to be illuminated nor simply its opposite; because it is seen through luminosity, a set of four directions arises there.

rows.gloss: the Lord whose body is the five mantras
is the lord of all directions

items.question: How does the five-mantra Lord relate to the other cosmic lords of the directions?
premises: The Lord with a five-mantra body is the sovereign of all directions.
After him, Īśa, Rudra, Viṣṇu, and Brahmā are established in sequence.
The directional order extends through this hierarchy of lords.
items.inference: The governance of directions is articulated through a descending hierarchy beginning with the five-mantra Lord.
uncertainties: The exact hierarchical nuance between Nātha and Īśa depends on the broader doctrinal context.
items.plain_english: Thus the Lord whose body is the five mantras is the sovereign of all directions, and after him Īśa, Rudra, Viṣṇu, and Brahmā are likewise established.

rows.gloss: because of fitness for upward manifestation, of Viṣṇu and of Brahmā
the sources of creation and maintenance

items.question: Why do Viṣṇu and Brahmā lack a fifth face in this scheme?
premises: Viṣṇu and Brahmā are associated with creation and maintenance, which involve differentiation.
A fifth face would correspond to a higher mode of upward manifestation.
Their functions do not extend to that fifth, transcendent mode.
items.inference: Viṣṇu and Brahmā do not possess a fifth face because their roles remain within differentiated manifestation.
uncertainties: dhātuḥ here is taken as referring to Brahmā, the creator.
items.plain_english: Viṣṇu and Brahmā do not have a fifth face, because they are powers of differentiation concerned with maintenance and creation, not with that higher upward manifestation.

items.question: What would happen if Viṣṇu and Brahmā were given a fifth face?
premises: Their directional division arises from four faces.
The fifth face belongs to a higher, non-differentiated mode.
Assuming that fifth face would contradict their proper nature.
items.inference: Viṣṇu and Brahmā remain four-faced because taking on a fifth would negate their own differentiated functions.
uncertainties: yujitve is read in sense as a conditional gerundive/absolutive formation; the exact morphology is compressed.
items.plain_english: Their division of directions comes from four faces; if a fifth were joined to them, those two would abandon their own nature.

rows.gloss: the power of knowledge of the Lord
having a nature dense with light

items.question: How is the division of directions manifested within the cosmic egg?
premises: The Lord's power of knowledge operates within the cosmic egg.
The sun is a dense manifestation of light.
The sun divides the directions through its illuminating activity.
items.inference: Within the cosmos, the sun functions as the Lord's knowledge-power in establishing the division of directions.
uncertainties: The identification of ravi with jñānaśakti is doctrinal and may be read as manifestation rather than strict identity.
items.plain_english: Therefore, even within the cosmic egg, the Lord's power of knowledge, appearing as the sun dense with light, makes the division of the directions.

items.question: How are east and west determined by the sun's observable movement?
premises: At the equinox, the sun's rising point is clearly observed.
The place where the sun first appears is called east.
The direction of its shadow indicates the opposite side, called west.
items.inference: East and west are determined empirically by the sun's appearance and the direction of its shadow.
uncertainties: The verse assumes a standard observational setup not fully described in the text.
items.plain_english: For example, at the equinox, where the sun is first seen is called east, and where its shadow falls is called west.

rows.gloss: when it is about to go there

items.question: How is the southern direction identified from the sun's course?
premises: The sun's movement provides a reference for left and right.
What lies to the sun's left in its course is identified as south.
The south is associated with the sun's fierce, blazing heat.
items.inference: The southern direction is defined by the sun's path and characterized by its intense heat.
uncertainties: The orientation assumes a particular observer-facing convention implicit in the tradition.
items.plain_english: As the sun moves on its course, what lies to its left is the south, where it shines with fierce rays as if blazing intensely.

rows.gloss: what is in front of that

items.question: Why is the northern side described as gentle rather than dark?
premises: The side in front of the southern reference is called the left or north.
It is slightly touched by the sun's light.
Because it receives some light, it is gentle but not devoid of illumination.
items.inference: The north is characterized as gentle because it receives moderated, not absent, light.
uncertainties: somyaṃ may also evoke a lunar or soothing quality beyond mere mildness.
items.plain_english: What lies in front of that is the left, slightly touched by its light; therefore it is gentle, yet not without light.

rows.gloss: where that one goes to setting
there is the seeing of the earlier light

items.question: How is the western direction defined at sunset?
premises: The place where the sun sets is established as the west.
Even in the west, traces of earlier light may still be seen.
Directional identity is tied to the sun's observable course.
items.inference: The west is defined by the sun's setting, while still bearing the after-presence of its light.
uncertainties: The final clause may also imply a ritual or contemplative orientation toward the fading eastern light.
items.plain_english: Where the sun sets is established as the west; and even there, for some, the earlier light can still be seen.
